results.controlIntent: (a) In accordance with [Selection: a role-based access scheme; an attribute-based access scheme], establish and administer privileged user accounts; (b) Watch privileged role or attribute assignments; (c) Watch changes to roles or attributes; and (d) Take away access when privileged role or attribute assignments are no longer appropriate.

judgment.rationale:
AC-2(7).v3 requires: (a) establishing and administering privileged accounts under a role-based or attribute-based scheme; (b) monitoring privileged role/attribute assignments; (c) monitoring changes to those roles/attributes; and (d) revoking access when assignments are no longer appropriate. Evidence from both collectors reveals multiple failures across all four sub-requirements:

**Sub-requirement (a) — Privileged account establishment/administration:**
The endpoint's IAM execution role (`SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`, ARN: `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`) carries two wildcard policies: `s3:*` on `*` (all S3 actions on all resources, including cross-account) and `sagemaker:*` on `*` (all SageMaker actions on all resources). This is the opposite of a properly administered, least-privilege privileged role. The role name ("Generic") further suggests it is shared and not scoped to this endpoint's specific needs — not consistent with a disciplined role-based or attribute-based access scheme.

**Sub-requirement (b) — Monitoring privileged role/attribute assignments:**
CloudTrail shows that `data-scientist-jdoe` performed `CreateEndpoint` on 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z — **two hours before** the model registry approval at 09:00 (noted in the event). This means a privileged deployment action was executed without any gating or monitoring that would have caught the out-of-order sequence. No evidence of automated alerting or review of role assignments was found.

**Sub-requirement (c) — Monitoring changes to roles/attributes:**
The `UpdateEndpoint` event on 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z (hotfix by `data-scientist-jdoe`) has no corresponding registry entry, indicating that privileged changes to the endpoint are not being tracked against an authoritative change-control record. There is no evidence of change monitoring tied to role or attribute assignments.

**Sub-requirement (d) — Revoking access when no longer appropriate:**
No evidence of any access revocation process, periodic access review, or automated de-provisioning was found in either the IAM role configuration or the CloudTrail event history.

In summary, the privileged role is over-broad and generic, privileged actions are being taken outside of approved change-control windows, changes are not being monitored against authoritative records, and there is no evidence of access revocation processes. All four sub-requirements of AC-2(7).v3 are unmet.
gaps: No IAM Access Analyzer or AWS Config rule data available to assess continuous monitoring of role assignments
No evidence of periodic access reviews (e.g., AWS IAM Access Advisor usage reports) to confirm or deny sub-requirement (d) revocation processes
No SageMaker Model Registry approval workflow configuration available to fully characterize the change-control gate
No evidence of SCPs (Service Control Policies) or permission boundaries that might compensate for the overly broad role policies
Human attestation needed to confirm whether out-of-band processes (e.g., manual reviews, ticketing systems) exist for monitoring and revoking privileged access

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped
